items.title: Joseph Thomas Interview, 1960-09-29
items.q: Then I played with Kid René years ago. I played with John Lewis, played with John Lewis, a ticket seat. So Kid René got me to play with him.

ctx.x: Do you remember any of the early dance bands that you hear when you were younger? Like on a wagon or anything, advertising maybe?

Yes, I remember Kid Punch, Kid René, Buddy Petit, Chris Kelly. I remember all of them. Right there on Orleans, they used to have a, it was an open lot, but they had built a platform on Orleans and White. That was years ago. And Kid Punch Band used to play back there. For dancing? Yes, uh-huh. Yeah, they used to have some fun. Is that a little park or not? But I was too, you know, to be going in, so all I'd do is stand on our side and listen. I had them play, you know, stand by the fence and get them. That would…
How did that music in those days compare with the music that you hear now? Was it very similar or pretty much the same or different?

items.title: Joseph Thomas Interview, 1960-09-29
items.q: Well like Bunk Johnson I didn't know him too much. Yeah. ... Kid Punch, Buddy Petit, Kid Rene.

ctx.x: Uh huh. Yes. Well I'll tell you them boys like I said them boys were really wonderful. That all them trumpet players you know they really knew what they were doing. Kid Punch, Buddy Petit, Kid Rene. Well like Bunk Johnson I didn't know him too much. Yeah.
Do you remember Joe Oliver? Did you ever hear him before he went north? No. No I don't. Or Armstrong did you hear him when you were a kid? You'd be pretty young.
